drivers.lead: Buemi and Hartley have shared the record since 2022, when both reached three in the same car; a fourth came in the 2023 finale and a fifth at Monza in 2026
drivers.note: Before 2022 nobody had won more than two, so the record has only ever belonged to these two men — and it moved to both of them at once, because Sébastien Buemi and Brendon Hartley were sharing the #8 Toyota when it happened. The fourth came together too, with a lights-to-flag win at the 8 Hours of Bahrain on 4 November 2023, and so did the fifth, with tenth place at the 6 Hours of Monza on 8 November 2026. Neither run is consecutive. Buemi's five are 2014, the 2018-19 super season, 2022, 2023 and 2026, all with Toyota; Hartley's are 2015 and 2017 with Porsche's LMP1 team and then 2022, 2023 and 2026 with Toyota, which makes him the rarer case of a champion for two manufacturers. Ryō Hirakawa has three, all won in the same car as the record holders, and five drivers sit on two. That is what makes five hard: the title is shared by a crew of three, so holding the seat is not enough — both team-mates have to keep working too.

teams.lead: Toyota went outright ahead in 2023, stretched it to five in 2024, lost the run to Ferrari in 2025 and won it back in 2026 for a sixth
teams.note: Six is a smaller number than Toyota's record suggests, and the reason is a rule rather than a result. For the 2018-19 and 2019-20 seasons the FIA replaced the top-class manufacturers' championship with a teams' title, because the award required at least two registered manufacturers and Toyota was the only one left in LMP1 after Audi and Porsche walked away. Toyota won both of those teams' championships and neither is counted here. Its six are 2014, then four straight from 2021 to 2024 once the Hypercar rules brought the grid back, and 2026. Porsche is closest on three — 2015, 2016 and 2017, consecutive, and none since its LMP1 programme closed — and Audi has two, from the championship's first two seasons. Ferrari's 2025 title was the marque's first in the top class of world endurance racing since 1972, and the only one anyone has taken off Toyota since the Hypercar era began.
